context.model: 1-2B local next-edit-suggestion model for R (pharma/biostat users, VS Code)
context.prompt: file above cursor + typed partial + file below cursor + recent diffs (event)
context.target_convention: suffix-only: the model predicts ONLY what comes after the cursor; cursor is placed at the first changed line; nothing above the cursor is ever re-emitted (v5 user-confirmed convention)
context.rscript_available: /usr/bin/Rscript, R 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) — execution validators permitted but used only as optional construction-time filters (roxygen_examples)
context.difficulty_rule: Prime Intellect: random/garbage output must score ~0 (stated per family in difficulty_knobs.random_fails); strong model must score well before training; no-op and shuffled-target controls must both score ~0 at build time

corpus.tarballs: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs/*.tar.gz (14,202; python-tarfile streaming member reads per format_propagation.py; members confirmed to include NAMESPACE, DESCRIPTION, tests/testthat/*.R, vignettes|doc/*.Rmd)

context.row_conventions: edit-pair schema (prefix/region_old/region_new/cursor_idx/event_diff/note) per scenarios.py; per-family caps 4-6k rows, per-package caps 2-4; 3% package holdout per family for eval_scenarios; char budget 5850 (assembler 6000 gate)
context.library_key_mapping: this file is a MULTI-PROPOSAL design document (16 proposals), not a single loadable CaseSpec: load_case()/--spec target one case per file. Mapping to cases/spec.py REQUIRED_KEYS when splitting a proposal into its own spec file: prompt_template -> prompt_templates, sampler -> parameter_sampler {name, params}, corpus_source -> {selector, ...}, validator -> {name, params}, target_construction -> {kind, ...}; difficulty_knobs.random_fails and novelty_note carry over as-is (novelty_note is already a spec key).

triage_gemini_12.reason: argument_list FIM already sampled by ast_fim (48% of 276k rows); a new constructor would double-count; tag + mixture oversample gets the SDTM/ADaM column-selection bias for free
standalone volume far too thin; proposed export-resolution validator passes any well-formed call (random-fails violated); the general chain-next-link capability subsumes it at high volume
fills tests gap; GT = author's exact suffix from real tests/testthat files; Gemini's structural-only validator demoted to a floor under the exact gate
reverse-strip construction makes GT the exact corpus line (tier 1, no R namespace lookup needed); upgraded to the propagation pattern that scored 92% for rename
class definitions usually live in other files/packages (Bioconductor S4 not in corpus); same-file setClass+@ co-occurrence too rare; validator cannot resolve slots reliably
whole-bracket completion is low-learnability author-choice FIM; the exactly-checkable edit is the drop=FALSE insertion, which reuses _single_insert_before_close from na_rm_propagation
as.formula() accepts any valid formula so the proposed validator passes random output; exact-match to author covariate choice is unlearnable from local context — teaches confident hallucination
aes() completion is argument_list FIM; structural layer-parse check too weak (any call parses)

fills error-handling gap; corrected because WRAPPING forces re-indentation below cursor (retired whole-region convention); suffix-compliant version completes handler clauses at a cut inside an existing tryCatch
merged with stop()-message drafting: one capability to a 1-2B model; cli tag whitelist regex is a genuine tier-3 check garbage fails
closed 3-operator target space plus arbitrary RHS — a tiny classification dressed as completion; ast_fim body spans cover mid-expression continuation
real pharma value and exact GT but level order only partially inferable; forcats-volume moderate; ship after exact-tier families

mixture_actions.name: tidyselect_slice
mixture_actions.action: tag ast_fim rows whose argument_list span sits inside select/relocate/across() calls; oversample in mixture

mixture_actions.name: ggplot_aes_slice
mixture_actions.action: tag ast_fim rows whose span is the argument list of an aes() call; oversample in mixture

proposals.name: namespace_qualify_propagation
proposals.description: Explicit package:: qualification of bare function calls. The event shows the user restoring one `pkg::fun(` prefix in a file where all `pkg::` prefixes for one package were stripped; the target re-qualifies the next bare occurrence of a function from the same package. Teaches the FDA-submission convention of explicit namespaces over library() attachment.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = file lines above the target call (10-line window), typed partial = the target line up to the cursor placed immediately before the bare function identifier, suffix = rest of file below, event_diff = one-line diff restoring the previous `pkg::` prefix
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — files containing `pkg::` calls; pick packages whose functions are called with :: at least 3x in a file (dplyr, stats, utils, rlang heavy)
proposals.sampler: per file: choose ONE package p such that p appears as a namespace >= 3 times; strip every `p::` prefix in the file to build the prompt-side state; event = first stripped occurrence re-qualified; target = the next stripped occurrence (70% immediately-next, 30% random later occurrence, rename_propagation convention); per-package cap 3, family cap 5k
proposals.target_construction: region_old = the stripped line (bare `fun(`); region_new = the ORIGINAL corpus line verbatim (`pkg::fun(`) — GT is exact by construction because the corpus line exists; cursor at the byte offset of the bare identifier
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text: prediction must equal region_new exactly after rstrip-normalization; structural floor: tree-sitter parses the line and the qualified head resolves to a namespace_operator node. Insertion check: new == old with exactly one `pkg::` inserted at the cursor (a namespace twin of _single_token_edit)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: random text does not equal the exact original line (exact 0) and does not parse as a qualified call; a shuffled-target control predicts a different package's prefix and fails the one-insertion check; no-op (bare call unchanged) scores 0
knobs: distance: next-occurrence vs distant occurrence after the event
shadowing: exclude files where fun is also a base-R name (ambiguous) unless the event disambiguates
prefix length: 1-token functions vs long dashed names

proposals.novelty_note: No existing family edits call heads. rename_propagation renames identifiers, pipe_rewrite swaps operators; nothing teaches qualification. The event-teaches-target-repeats geometry is the exact pattern that hit 92% (rename) on held-out packages.

proposals.name: pipe_chain_link
proposals.description: Next link of a pipe chain. Cursor at end-of-line right after a `%>%` or `|>` operator; target = the next chain link line (the next call) verbatim. The gtsummary `tbl_summary() |> add_p() |> bold_labels()` CSR workflow, generalized to all chains (dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2 plot chains).
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = chain lines above (10-line window, always including the chain head so the data context is visible), typed partial = the line ending in the pipe operator with the cursor after it, suffix = file below (contains the REAL next line only in training GT sense — see target_construction), event_diff = empty (cold) or the previous link completed
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — multi-line pipe chains (pipe operator at end of line, RHS call starting the next line); tidy_packages() pre-scan first for density, random packages for breadth
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter walk for binary_operator chains whose operator ends a line and whose RHS begins the following line; require >= 2 remaining links; single-line calls only per link; cap links at 300 chars; per-package cap 3, family cap 5k; exclude byte ranges already published by ast_fim when its span map is recoverable (else accept mild overlap)
proposals.target_construction: region_old = [the pipe-operator line with cursor at line end]; region_new = [the pipe line + the next link line]; the model-visible target is the suffix after the cursor = the next link line(s) (max 2 lines), verbatim from the file
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text on the emitted link; structural floor: tree-sitter parses the link as a call node (garbage fragments fail)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage neither equals the author's link nor parses as a call; a wrong-but-valid verb (add_overall vs add_p) fails exact and scores ~0 line-F1 because verb+args differ wholesale; no-op emits nothing = 0
knobs: chain position: 2nd link (verb highly predictable from the head) vs deep link
chain family: dplyr data chains vs ggplot layer chains vs gtsummary-style table chains (stratify and report per stratum)
event on/off: cold completion vs previous-link-shown propagation

proposals.novelty_note: finish_block completes function bodies from block START; ast_fim samples argument_list spans mid-call; neither teaches line-granular next-link continuation of a chain — the single most repeated edit shape in tidyverse reporting code. Absorbs gemini#2 (gtsummary) as a stratum instead of a too-thin standalone family.

proposals.name: pkg_metadata_sync
proposals.description: Package metadata maintenance: (a) NAMESPACE — after adding a function, insert its export() (or importFrom/S3method) line at the alphabetically correct position; (b) DESCRIPTION — after first using pkg:: / library(pkg) in R/, insert the package under Imports:. Both constructed by reverse-stripping a real entry from real tarball NAMESPACE/DESCRIPTION files, so GT is exact.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = NAMESPACE/DESCRIPTION lines above the insertion slot (for NAMESPACE typically the whole sorted file head; for DESCRIPTION the Imports: section), typed partial = empty line at the insertion slot with the cursor, suffix = remaining file lines, event_diff = the code-side change (function definition line added to R/<file>.R for (a); first pkg:: usage line added for (b))
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs — NAMESPACE and DESCRIPTION members (confirmed present in every sampled tarball), streamed via python tarfile (format_propagation infra); restrict (a) to alphabetically-sorted NAMESPACE files (roxygen2 output; measure sortedness rate first — open item)
proposals.sampler: per package: read NAMESPACE + DESCRIPTION once; for (a) pick an export line whose defining function is locatable in the normalized R/ tree; for (b) pick an Imports entry whose package appears as pkg:: in R/; strip it; per-package cap 2 (one per kind), family cap 4k
proposals.target_construction: (a) region_old = ['' (the stripped slot)], region_new = ['export(<fn>)'] exactly as the real line read; (b) region_new = ['    <pkg>'] exactly as read (with its real indentation); cursor at slot start; the model-visible target is that inserted line plus nothing else
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact single-line insertion: line matches ^(export|importFrom|S3method)\(...)\)$ or ^\s+[A-Za-z][\w.]*$ AND lands at the alphabetically correct position among the surviving lines (insertion twin of _assert_doc_region)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage matches neither the entry regex nor the sorted-position check; a valid-but-wrong entry (export of a different function) fails exact match and the position check; no-op = 0 (slot stays empty)
knobs: neighborhood distance: insert next to a near-alphabet neighbor vs middle of a long file
kind mix: export vs importFrom vs S3method vs DESCRIPTION Imports
event salience: function def shown as event vs only its name in the diff header

proposals.novelty_note: Only format_propagation touches non-.R files (and only R/ members). DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE sync is the roxygen2 workflow every package developer repeats; fills the named DESCRIPTION gap. No existing family edits package metadata.

proposals.name: expectation_completion
proposals.description: Inside a test_that() block: after setup lines (assignments, fixture calls), complete the expect_* assertion. Cursor right after the typed `expect_` partial or after `expect_equal(`; target = the author's exact expectation call, from real CRAN test files.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = the test_that header + setup lines above (up to 15 lines), typed partial = the partial expect_ token or open call with cursor, suffix = remaining test block + file below, event_diff = a previously-completed expectation in the same block (propagation flavor) or empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs — tests/testthat/*.R members (confirmed present in a large subset of tarballs), streamed via python tarfile; tree-sitter-r parse of test files
proposals.sampler: extract test_that blocks via tree-sitter; keep single-line expect_* calls preceded by >= 1 setup line inside the block; prefer blocks with >= 2 expectations (event target pairs); per-package cap 3, family cap 5k
proposals.target_construction: cut the file at a deterministic point: after the `expect_` prefix (medium) or after `expect_equal(res, ` (hard); region_old = the cut line; region_new = the author's full line verbatim; cursor at the cut column; visible target = the line suffix from the cursor
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text as the gate; tier 2 structural floor: tree-sitter parses the completion as a call whose callee matches ^expect_ and arg count >= 1 — the floor ALONE is intentionally insufficient (any well-formed expect call passes); document that only the exact gate scores

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage does not parse as an expect_* call (floor) and equals neither the author's call (exact 0); a valid-but-wrong expectation (expect_true vs expect_equal) fails the exact gate — partial line-F1 credit only for shared prefix, ~0 in practice; no-op = 0
knobs: cut depth: after `expect_` vs after `expect_equal(obj, ` vs mid-argument
setup richness: typed assignment visible (res <-) vs only the function call
expectation class stratification: expect_equal / expect_s3_class / expect_error / expect_snapshot

proposals.novelty_note: Fills the named tests gap. No existing family emits test code of any kind; testthat blocks live outside R/ so ast_fim/finish_block never see them. Distinct from testthat_skeleton (which drafts the whole block from a function).

proposals.name: trycatch_handler_completion
proposals.description: Complete the condition handlers of an existing tryCatch / withCallingHandlers call: cursor right after the comma following the guarded expression block; target = the author's handler clauses (`error = function(e) {...}, warning = function(w) {...}`) up to the closing paren.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = function context above + `tryCatch({` + the guarded expression block, typed partial = the line ending `}, ` with cursor after the comma+space, suffix = code after the tryCatch call, event_diff = empty (cold idiom completion)
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — tryCatch/withCallingHandlers calls whose expression block and handlers are both parseable; single-file, cap handler clause at 8 lines
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter walk for calls named tryCatch/withCallingHandlers with >= 1 handler argument of the form name = function(e){...}; require the call to span >= 3 lines; per-package cap 2, family cap 4k
proposals.target_construction: cut immediately after `}, ` following the expression argument; region_old = that line; region_new = the author's remaining argument lines verbatim through the call's closing paren; cursor at the cut column
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text as gate; tier 2 structural floor: completion parses and contains named arguments where each handler name in {error, warning, message, finally} maps to a function of exactly 1 formal

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage neither equals the author's clauses nor parses as handler arguments (unbalanced braces fail the floor); a swapped handler body (warning's body under error=) parses but fails exact — acknowledged multi-valid target, so per-family eval also reports structural-pass rate separately from exact
knobs: handler count: single error handler vs error+warning vs +finally
body style: rethrow (rlang::abort) vs fallback value vs logging side-effect
guard complexity: expression block length 1 vs 5+ lines

proposals.novelty_note: Fills the named error-handling gap; nothing existing emits condition-handling code. Deliberately completion-NOT-wrapping: wrapping would re-indent the file below the cursor, the retired whole-region convention (gemini#9 corrected).

proposals.name: drop_false_propagation
proposals.description: Insert `drop = FALSE` into matrix-like `[` subsetting calls. The event adds it to one bracket call in a function; the target adds it to the next qualifying call — the exact geometry of na_rm_propagation, reusing its validator.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = 10-line window above, typed partial = the target line with cursor at the insertion column (immediately before the closing `]`), suffix = file below, event_diff = one-line diff adding `, drop = FALSE` to the previous call
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — files where >= 2 single-line `[` calls take 2 arguments (i,j form) and lack drop; prefer files that already use drop = FALSE elsewhere (style-affine authors)
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter subset nodes for `[` with >= 2 args, single-line, no drop= present, closing `]` locatable; pair event/target within the same function body first, same file as fallback (na_rm grouping logic reused); per-package cap 3, family cap 4k
proposals.target_construction: insert `, drop = FALSE` before the closing bracket at the exact column; region_old/new = the target line before/after; cursor at the insertion column
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact: _single_insert_before_close(old, new, ', drop = FALSE') generalized from ')' to ']' (validator code reused verbatim otherwise)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: any prediction that is not the old line plus exactly one insertion before `]` fails the validator (count+position check); garbage text breaks the bracket parse; no-op = 0
knobs: call shape: df[cond, cols] vs mat[i, j] vs x[i, , drop=FALSE] partially-typed
pairing distance: same summarise-style block vs same function vs same file
distractors: calls that legitimately want drop=TRUE are excluded by the corpus filter (only construct from authors who wrote FALSE)

proposals.novelty_note: na_rm_propagation appends a stat-argument; this inserts a subsetting-flag in bracket geometry — different node type, same proven validator. Fills the regulatory-matrix-coercion bug class (PK/PD) named in gemini#6, minus its unlearnable whole-bracket-completion framing.

proposals.name: format_string_completion
proposals.description: Complete string-literal-first arguments: the format string of sprintf/formatC, the pattern of sub/gsub/grepl/grep, the template of glue. Cursor right after the opening quote or after `("`; target = the literal plus remaining args to end of line.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = 10-line window above (includes the variables the string references), typed partial = the call up to the opening quote with cursor after it, suffix = file below, event_diff = empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — single-line calls to sprintf, formatC, format, glue, glue_data, sub, gsub, grepl, grep whose target argument is a double-quoted string literal without embedded quotes
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter call walk; require the literal to be the FIRST argument (or the pattern= named arg for grep-family); line length <= 300; per-package cap 3, family cap 5k; skip spans published by ast_fim when recoverable
proposals.target_construction: cut at the column after the opening `"`; region_old = the cut line; region_new = the author's line verbatim; visible target = literal content + closing quote + remaining args
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text; structural floor (tier 2): the literal's escapes are balanced/valid, and for sprintf the count of printf specifiers (%d %s %f %.Nf %g) equals the count of following comma-separated args — garbage breaks escape/specifier consistency before exact comparison even runs

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: random text fails the escape/specifier consistency check and the exact gate; a fluent-but-wrong format string (%d vs %.4f) fails exact though it may pass the floor — the floor is a garbage filter, not a scorer; no-op = 0
knobs: cut depth: after opening quote vs after `%,` inside the literal vs mid-literal (hard)
fn family: sprintf (specifier-constrained) vs grepl (regex-constrained) vs glue (brace-constrained)
context availability: referenced variables assigned in the prefix vs not

proposals.novelty_note: String-literal content is where small FIM models are weakest; ast_fim span kinds (argument_list/function_body/top_level_block) do not isolate string-initiated completions. CSR code is saturated with format strings (rounding, percentages, footnotes).

proposals.name: rmd_chunk_scaffold
proposals.description: R Markdown chunk headers: after the user types the fence `` ```{r ` , complete the chunk label + options through end of the header line (e.g. `sumtab, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}`).
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = preceding prose/chunk lines from the Rmd (10-line window; include the previous chunk's header when present), typed partial = the fence line `` ```{r `` with cursor after it, suffix = the chunk's code body + rest of the Rmd, event_diff = a previous chunk header completed (propagation flavor) or empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs — vignettes/*.Rmd and doc/*.Rmd members (confirmed present in roughly half of sampled tarballs), streamed via python tarfile; line-regex scan (Rmd has no R parser; tree-sitter not applicable)
proposals.sampler: Rmd files with >= 2 r-chunk headers; header line <= 200 chars; label non-empty; per-package cap 2, family cap 4k; pair consecutive chunks for the event flavor
proposals.target_construction: cut after `` ```{r `` (sometimes after the label comma for a harder cut); region_old = the fence prefix; region_new = the full header line verbatim; cursor at the cut column
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact line; structural floor: header completes to `^```\{r[^,}]*(, [A-Za-z][\w.]+=[^,}]+)*\}$` with knitr-vocabulary option names (echo, eval, include, message, warning, results, fig.width, fig.height, fig.path, cache, child)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage fails the header regex (unbalanced fence/options); a valid-but-wrong option set passes the floor but fails exact — floor is the garbage filter; no-op leaves an unterminated chunk = 0
knobs: cut depth: after `{r` vs after the label + comma
chunk role: setup chunks (knitr::opts_chunk) vs figure chunks (fig.*) vs hidden-info chunks (echo=FALSE)
event on/off: previous header shown vs cold

proposals.novelty_note: Zero Rmd coverage anywhere in the mixture (ast_fim walks .R only). CSR authoring is Rmd-first; the echo/message/warning triplet is arguably the most-repeated line in clinical reporting.

proposals.name: testthat_skeleton
proposals.description: Draft a test_that block from a function: prompt shows the function's roxygen + signature (+ body head), target is the author's actual test_that block for that function — the 'write my tests' GxP action.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = the function's roxygen block + signature (body head if budget allows), typed partial = empty line at the end of a test file with cursor, suffix = following test blocks if any, event_diff = empty or a sibling test block for another function of the same package (propagation flavor)
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs — pairing tests/testthat/test-*.R blocks with exported functions from the same package's normalized R/ tree
proposals.sampler: extract test_that blocks (tree-sitter); for each exported function f, select the block with the highest count of f references (deterministic); require >= 1 reference; block capped at 30 lines / 2500 chars; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k
proposals.target_construction: region_old = ['']; region_new = the test_that block lines verbatim (header quote included); cursor at the empty line; visible target = the whole block (pure suffix — nothing above the cursor is re-emitted)
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text as gate; tier 2 structural floor: parses, contains >= 1 expect_* call, references f by name

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage equals neither the block nor its structure; a valid-but-different test block fails exact (multi-valid drafting target — report structural-pass separately, judge at eval time like comment_drafting)
knobs: function visibility: full body below cursor (suffix contains it, roxygen_drafting geometry) vs signature only
block size: <= 10 lines vs up to 30
test kind stratification: pure-function tests vs snapshot-adjacent vs fixture-dependent (skip the latter if setup fixtures are external)

proposals.novelty_note: The drafting counterpart of expectation_completion: no existing family generates test code; fills the named tests gap from the other direction (function -> block, not block-internal completion).

proposals.name: lambda_shorthand_migration
proposals.description: Modernize `function(x) expr` to the R 4.1 lambda shorthand `\(x) expr`. The event rewrites one single-expression anonymous function; the target rewrites the next — pipe_rewrite's exact style-migration pattern for the other live base-R migration.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = 10-line window above, typed partial = the target line with cursor at the `function` token, suffix = file below, event_diff = one-line diff rewriting the previous occurrence
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — files with >= 2 anonymous `function(<simple args>) <single-line expr>` definitions (no defaults, no braces, body a single expression), typical in map/lapply/`function(x) ...` positions
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter function_definition nodes without braced body, parameters without defaults, fully single-line; require the parent context to be a call argument (anonymous use); per-package cap 3, family cap 4k
proposals.target_construction: replace the `function(` token with `\(` leaving args and body byte-identical; region_old/new = the line before/after; cursor at the `function` token start
proposals.validator: tier 1 mechanical swap (pipe_rewrite twin): new == old with exactly one occurrence of `function(` replaced by `\(`, parens balanced, remainder byte-identical

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: any non-swap text fails the one-substring-replacement check exactly as tampered pipe_rewrite rows fail today; no-op = 0
knobs: arg count: 1 vs 2 args
context verb: purrr map/modify vs base apply family vs stats
density: adjacent lines vs distant occurrences

proposals.novelty_note: pipe_rewrite covers %>% -> |>; nothing covers function() -> \() — the other style migration R developers actually perform en masse. Fills the named style-migration gap.

proposals.name: condition_message_drafting
proposals.description: Draft condition messages: the message argument of stop/warning/message, rlang::abort/inform, cli::cli_abort/cli_alert_* — including cli glue classes ({.var}, {.val}, {.cls}) and inline interpolation of in-scope variables.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = the guarding if() and surrounding checks (10-line window), typed partial = the call up to the opening quote / c( with cursor, suffix = file below, event_diff = empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — stop/warning/message/rlang::abort/rlang::inform/cli::cli_abort/cli::cli_alert_* calls with a first-argument string or character vector; single-line or vector-of-strings targets capped 5 lines
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter call walk keyed on callee names; require an enclosing if/stopifnot guard in the same function for context; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k
proposals.target_construction: cut after `stop(` + opening quote (or after `c(` for cli vectors); region_old = cut line; region_new = author's argument(s) verbatim; cursor at the cut column
proposals.validator: tier 3 structural: string parses (balanced quotes/escapes), glue braces balanced, every {.cls} tag from the cli whitelist ({.val .var .str .cls .arg .fn .emph .strong .code .field}); exact-text reported alongside but free-text semantics scored only by the calibrated judge at eval (comment_drafting precedent)

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage breaks quote/brace balance or uses a non-whitelisted {.tag} — fails structurally; no-op = 0; note honestly that a grammatical wrong message can pass the structural tier, which is why eval uses the judge
knobs: API family: base stop() vs rlang::abort(class=) vs cli vector messages
interpolation density: 0 vs 1-3 {var} references to in-scope names
guard visibility: the if-condition naming the failure visible in prefix

proposals.novelty_note: Fills the named logging/message gap (merged gemini#10 + stop()-message drafting). comment_drafting judges comments; nothing drafts messages. pharmaverse tooling mandates structured messages.

proposals.name: s3_method_insertion
proposals.description: Add the next S3 method for a generic the file already implements: after print.myclass exists (event), insert summary.myclass / `[.myclass` at top level (target) — the 'make generic() work for my class' edit.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = the file's existing methods for the generic + class-assigning constructor above, typed partial = empty top-level line with cursor where the method belongs, suffix = following top-level definitions, event_diff = multi-line diff adding the previous method definition (format_propagation multi-line event format)
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — files defining >= 2 top-level `generic.class <- function` sharing a generic (print/summary/plot/as.data.frame/[/format/str dominance)
proposals.sampler: regex+tree-sitter: top-level binary_operator definitions whose LHS matches ^[a-zA-Z.][\w.]*\.[\w.]+$; group by generic; require >= 2 in file; reverse-strip method k as target, method k-1 as event; target def capped 20 lines; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k
proposals.target_construction: region_old = the stripped slot (empty line / adjacent def line); region_new = the stripped method's full definition verbatim; cursor at the slot
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text + structural name check: completion parses as a function definition whose LHS shares the event's generic prefix

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage is not a function definition / LHS pattern breaks; a valid method for the WRONG generic fails the name check; no-op = 0
knobs: generic popularity: print/summary (conventional signatures) vs niche generics
signature copying: event method shows the conventional (x, ...) signature to imitate vs not
def size: <= 5 lines vs up to 20

proposals.novelty_note: rename_propagation renames within a function; nothing adds sibling top-level definitions. S3 is the pharma ADaM-class tooling workhorse (gemini#5's S4 sibling dropped for volume; S3 is CRAN-native and abundant).

proposals.name: assertion_insertion
proposals.description: Insert the next input-check assertion (stopifnot(...) or checkmate assert_*) at the head of a function. The event adds one check; the target inserts the next — error-handling idiom coverage complementary to tryCatch.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = function signature + already-present checks above, typed partial = empty line at the checks' position with cursor, suffix = function body below, event_diff = one-line diff inserting the previous stopifnot check
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — function bodies whose head (first 5 statements) contains >= 2 stopifnot(...) single-line calls (or checkmate::assert_* calls)
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter function bodies; collect leading stopifnot/assert lines; reverse-strip one as target, the preceding one as event; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k
proposals.target_construction: region_old = the line at the insertion slot; region_new = that line preceded by the stripped check line (single-line insertion); cursor at the slot — visible target = check line + the old line's start (insertion geometry)
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact single-line insertion (doc_sync _assert_doc_region twin): new == old + exactly one inserted line that parses as a stopifnot/assert_* call

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage is not an exact one-line insertion of a parseable check call; a wrong-but-valid check fails exact; no-op = 0
knobs: API: stopifnot vs checkmate::assert_* vsrlang::is_installed guards
argument visibility: the checked parameter obvious from the signature vs derived
check complexity: simple !is.null(x) vs length(x) == nrow(df) cross-references

proposals.novelty_note: na_rm appends an argument to a call; assertion_insertion inserts a STATEMENT at a function head — different edit geometry, fills the defensive-validation half of the error-handling gap.

proposals.name: factor_level_completion
proposals.description: Complete level specifications in factor()/forcats::fct_* calls: after the variable argument, the ordered level vector (Screening, Baseline, Week 4, ...) or na level mapping.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = 10-line window above (includes the data context where levels appear), typed partial = the call up to the comma after the first argument with cursor, suffix = file below, event_diff = empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — factor(...levels=...) and forcats::fct_relevel/fct_rev/fct_na_value_to_level calls with explicit string-vector levels, single-line, via tidy_packages() pre-scan
proposals.sampler: tree-sitter calls to factor/forcats::fct_* with >= 2 string-literal level args; cap line 300 chars; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k
proposals.target_construction: cut after the first argument + comma; region_old = cut line; region_new = author's line verbatim; cursor at the cut column
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact text; tier 2 floor: completion parses, level args are string literals

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage fails parse/exact; a valid-but-reordered level list fails exact (ORDER is the semantics — this is the family's point); no-op = 0
knobs: level-source salience: levels literal appears elsewhere in the prefix (tabulation code) vs not
call family: base factor vs forcats

proposals.novelty_note: gemini#12 kept at wave 2: exact GT and real CSR value (visit/arm ordering), but level inventories are only partially inferable — ship after the tier-1 families prove the pattern.

proposals.name: roxygen_examples
proposals.description: Draft the @examples block: cursor inside a roxygen block at the position where @examples belongs; target = the author's examples stanza. Optionally filtered at construction time by EXECUTING the example in a fresh R env (Rscript 4.6.1 available) — execution is a construction filter, never the training-time gate.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = the roxygen block above the insertion point (title/params) with the function signature + body head visible in the suffix below, typed partial = the last roxygen line above the slot with cursor at its end, suffix = the function definition, event_diff = empty
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/normalized — the 47k rich-roxygen functions already identified for doc_sync/roxygen_drafting; emit only when the block contains @examples with >= 2 code lines
proposals.sampler: roxygen block walk (roxygen_drafting infra); target = the @examples sub-block only, capped 12 lines; per-package cap 2, family cap 3k; dedup against roxygen_drafting rows (same function never emits both a whole-block row and an examples-only row)
proposals.target_construction: region_old = the roxygen window around the slot; region_new = window + the @examples lines inserted before @return/@export (doc_sync insertion geometry); cursor at the slot
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact insertion of the @examples stanza; tier 2 floor: inserted lines are roxygen `#'` code lines; optional tier 5 construction filter: Rscript -e 'parse the examples' or run with library(pkg) in a temp env — discard non-running examples

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage is not an exact insertion of #' -prefixed parseable R lines; wrong-but-valid examples fail exact; no-op = 0
knobs: function visibility: full body in suffix vs signature only
example complexity: pure-expression vs library(require) prelude

proposals.novelty_note: roxygen_drafting drafts WHOLE blocks from an empty line above the function; this targets the examples stanza specifically with mid-block cursor geometry (the mid_roxygen lesson). Wave 2 pending the overlap/dedup check with roxygen_drafting's emitted blocks.

proposals.name: news_entry
proposals.description: Draft the NEWS.md stanza for the release being prepared: event = DESCRIPTION Version bump; target = the release's own stanza (the tarball's top NEWS stanza, reverse-stripped). NOTE: the original multi-version time-travel recipe was killed by audit — 0 of the 14,202 tarballs are a second version of any package — so construction is single-version reverse-strip.
proposals.prompt_template: edit-pair: prefix = empty (cursor at top of NEWS.md) or the stripped slot above the second stanza, typed partial = empty line with cursor, suffix = the remaining (previous-release) stanzas, event_diff = DESCRIPTION 'Version: <prev> -> Version: <cur>' where prev is derived from the second stanza's header
proposals.corpus_source: /mnt/h/sepalith/tarballs — NEWS/NEWS.md members whose top stanza header contains the tarball's own DESCRIPTION Version and which have >= 2 stanzas (prev version derivable)
proposals.sampler: read NEWS + DESCRIPTION from one tarball pass; require top-stanza/version match and >= 2 bullet lines in the top stanza, cap 10; per-package cap 1, family cap 2k
proposals.target_construction: prompt-side NEWS = the file with its TOP stanza stripped; region_old = the stripped slot; region_new = the top stanza verbatim (header + bullets); cursor at the slot
proposals.validator: tier 1 exact stanza text; tier 2 floor: markdown heading containing the current version string + bullet lines

difficulty_knobs.random_fails: garbage fails the heading/bullet structure and exact; a plausible-but-wrong bullet list fails exact (semantics judge-only at eval — drafting family); no-op = 0
knobs: event richness: plain version bump vs bump + one-line diff summary of the code change
stanza length

proposals.novelty_note: Fills the named NEWS gap. Nobody's edit stream is more predictable in SHAPE and less in CONTENT — the exact gate trains the shape; a judge eval scores content. Wave 2: constructibility 2 until the multi-version tarball audit lands.

ranking.formula: score = value(1-5) x constructibility(1-5) x validator_exactness(1-5)
